subject: AlphaBank — Dedicated Premium tier throughput commitment (draft language + next steps)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Silva <marta.silva@alphabank.com>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@alphabank.com>, AlphaBank Procurement <procurement@alphabank.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 25, 2025 at 4:12 PM -0700
Subject: AlphaBank — Dedicated Premium tier throughput commitment (draft language + next steps)
Attachments: AlphaBank_Redwood_Dedicated_Premium_Throughput_SLO_Draft_v3.pdf; Redwood_Dedicated_Tiers_Overview_2025Q2.pdf

Hi Marta (cc Jonas),

Following up from last week’s security/SLA review, here’s the proposed packaging + the draft throughput commitment language we can put into the order form for AlphaBank.

1) Proposed tier + deployment shape
- Tier: Dedicated Premium
- Region: EU (Frankfurt)
- Deployment: Single-model Dedicated pool (pinned model + pinned runtime profile)
- Shape (proposed): H100 x 8 (or equivalent Redwood-managed Premium shape in-region)

2) Throughput commitment (what we will commit to in writing)
We propose committing to a “Committed Throughput Floor” for the dedicated deployment, measured at the Redwood API boundary.

Draft (plain-English summary):
- Redwood will provide a monthly throughput SLO for the Dedicated deployment such that, during Eligible Measurement Windows, the deployment’s throughput will meet or exceed the Committed Throughput Floor.
- If the SLO is not met, AlphaBank is eligible for service credits as described in the order form.

Draft metric (as reflected in the attached PDF):
- Metric: output_tokens_per_second (deployment-level), computed as total output tokens successfully generated divided by active generation wall-clock time.
- Measurement window: rolling 15-minute windows; compliance reported monthly.
- Target: 99% of Eligible Measurement Windows in the calendar month.
- Proposed Committed Throughput Floor (initial): 650 output tokens/sec for the deployment (subject to confirmation after the sizing benchmark using your target prompts/contexts).

3) Key conditions / exclusions (the ones we discussed)
We’ve kept these as tight as possible, but need a few standard exclusions so the metric can’t be skewed by client-side behavior:
- Customer-side backpressure or throttling (e.g., client cancels/halts streams early, or limits consumption rate).
- Requests outside agreed constraints (max context length, max output tokens, unsupported parameters).
- Model/version changes not coordinated through Redwood (i.e., if model pin is altered or customer requests an un-benchmarked variant).
- Planned maintenance windows with prior notice (as defined in the MSA / order form).

4) Next steps to finalize the number
To lock the Committed Throughput Floor, we should run a short sizing benchmark:
- Inputs from AlphaBank: (a) target model, (b) typical context length distribution, (c) typical output lengths, (d) concurrency profile (steady + peak), and (e) whether you require tool/function calling.
- Output from Redwood: final committed floor + the deployment configuration we are guaranteeing against.

If you confirm you’re aligned with “Dedicated Premium + throughput floor” as the structure, we can turn the attached draft into redline-ready contract language for Jonas.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated (Tiers & Commitments)
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

From: Marta Silva <marta.silva@alphabank.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@alphabank.com>, AlphaBank Procurement <procurement@alphabank.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 26, 2025 at 9:03 AM +0100
Subject: Re: AlphaBank — Dedicated Premium tier throughput commitment (draft language + next steps)

Hi Lauren,

Thank you — this is helpful.

A few points we need to clarify for internal approval:
1) When you say “650 output tokens/sec”, is that a minimum at all times or averaged? Our stakeholders are sensitive to “best effort” wording.
2) Can you confirm this is a written commitment for Premium (not just guidance)?
3) We need the credit / remedy language referenced in the order form. Is that in the attached PDF or separate?
4) On exclusions: please confirm that normal fluctuations in demand (bursts) do not invalidate eligibility. We will have weekly peaks.

Jonas may come back with edits, but if you can answer the above we can proceed with the benchmark inputs.

Best regards,
Marta Silva
Procurement Manager, Technology
AlphaBank

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Silva <marta.silva@alphabank.com>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@alphabank.com>, AlphaBank Procurement <procurement@alphabank.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 26, 2025 at 9:58 AM -0700
Subject: Re: AlphaBank — Dedicated Premium tier throughput commitment (draft language + next steps)

Hi Marta,

Great questions — quick answers inline.

1) Is “650 output tokens/sec” a minimum at all times?
It’s not an instantaneous guarantee; it’s an SLO measured over rolling 15-minute windows. The commitment is:
- In at least 99% of Eligible 15-minute windows in a calendar month, the measured throughput for the deployment is >= the Committed Throughput Floor.
We do it this way to avoid the guarantee being overly sensitive to second-by-second variance (GC, kernel selection, short-lived load changes).

2) Is this a written commitment for Premium?
Yes. Premium includes written throughput SLO language in the order form (and remedies), assuming the deployment stays within the agreed configuration (model/version/profile + request constraints).

3) Remedy / credit language
The attached PDF contains the proposed service credit framework as an exhibit (tiered credits based on severity/recurrence). If you’d prefer, we can also provide it as standalone order form language for Jonas to redline.

4) Do bursts invalidate eligibility?
No — normal demand peaks are expected. Bursts only become an issue if request patterns go outside the agreed constraints (e.g., repeated max-context + max-output requests far beyond the sizing assumptions), or if the client applies backpressure that materially changes the “active generation time” accounting.

Practically: if you share the weekly peak concurrency and the prompt/length distributions, we’ll size the deployment so peaks are within the committed profile.

If helpful, send the benchmark inputs as:
- 200 representative prompts (or an anonymized equivalent set)
- distributions for input tokens / output tokens
- peak concurrency targets

Once we run the benchmark, we’ll confirm the committed floor number for the pinned configuration and send a clean order form exhibit for legal review.

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren,

Understood on the 15-minute windows.

Please send the remedy language as standalone order form text (not just embedded in the PDF), as we need to circulate it for internal review. We will also want the exclusions to be explicitly enumerated in the same exhibit, with the “customer-side backpressure” clause defined in concrete terms.

Marta will coordinate sending the benchmark inputs early next week.

Regards,
Jonas Richter
Senior Legal Counsel (Technology)
AlphaBank
